Messages.Author: Joe Gorde
Messages.Body:
Okay, Thetmes the Assamite plays Death of My Conscience to give him 5
aggro hand damage. He then plays a Blur, for two additional strikes. His
opponent is a capacity-10 vampire, and doesn't prevent any damage. What
happens?

The opponent takes 5 aggro damage and immediately goes to torpor. You
don't even get to play the blur.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Joe Gorde <joeg...@ren.us.itd.umich.edu> writes:
>Okay, Thetmes the Assamite plays Death of My Conscience to give him 5
>aggro hand damage. He then plays a Blur, for two additional strikes. His
>opponent is a capacity-10 vampire, and doesn't prevent any damage. What
>happens?

The assamite never gets the chance to play Blur.
When the 10-cap goes to torpor (after the initial strike), combat is over.
Here's how it breaks down:

Combat
Play any "before range" cards...
Maneuver...
Choose strikes (one strike per combatant)
Resolve strikes
Gain additional strikes.
For each additional strike:
Choose strikes (one strike for each opponent who has available strikes).
Resolve strike.
Loop until neither opponent has any available strikes.
Press (and/or press-step effects)

If at any point of the above process one of the minions is no longer
ready (has been sent to torpor or burned), then combat ends at that
point (allowing for end-of-round effects like Pulled Fangs, Amaranth,
etc.)

Messages.Author: Michael Kelly
Messages.Body:
Joe Gorde wrote:
>
> Okay, Thetmes the Assamite plays Death of My Conscience to give him 5
> aggro hand damage. He then plays a Blur, for two additional strikes. His
> opponent is a capacity-10 vampire, and doesn't prevent any damage. What
> happens?
>

Combat ends after the first strike is resolved. When a vampire goes to topor
combat can not continue, Thetmas will never get a chance to even play his blur.
Even if a vampire is entitled to an additional strike without having to
play the blur, combat is over when one of the vampires goes to topor. That
is why many shrewd combat deck players will deal normal damage on the first
and possibly second strike and end up with an aggravated strike which will
burn the opposing vampire.

In your example, if Thetmas had owned a bastard sword, he could have
struck for 6 normal points of damage the first strike, played his blur, and
then struck for 5 points of aggravated damage using his hand strike on
the second strike and burned his opponent. Again, had he chosen the bastard
sword for his second strike there would have been no third strike as 12
points of normal dmage would have sent the vampire to topor.

Messages.Author: J. Andrew Lipscomb
Messages.Body:
In article <5cqjka$3...@lastactionhero.rs.itd.umich.edu>, Joe Gorde

<joeg...@ren.us.itd.umich.edu> wrote:

> Okay, Thetmes the Assamite plays Death of My Conscience to give him 5
> aggro hand damage. He then plays a Blur, for two additional strikes. His
> opponent is a capacity-10 vampire, and doesn't prevent any damage. What
> happens?

Can't be done. As soon as (say) Democritus gets hit with the first batch,
he's in torpor (or burned if he had less than 5 blood), and combat ends
before you get the chance to play additional strikes.
